title: Grateful Dead Live at Meadowlands Arena on 1988-04-01
lineage: DAT> ?> CD> SHN; via Raul; Seeded to etree by Peter Braverman

ai_review.summary: Excellent matrix mix captures a high‑energy 1988 show highlighted by a scorching Deal, soaring To Lay Me Down and an otherworldly Other One.
ai_review.review: The SBD‑>AUD matrix created by Peter Braverman delivers clear, punchy sound that lets the band’s 1988 fire shine through.  Fans rave about the first‑set power (To Lay Me Down, Ballad of a Thin Man) and a second‑set packed with Deal, Half‑Step, China→Rider and an epic Other One, all driven by Jerry’s blistering lead work and Brent’s soaring keyboards.  Minor quirks like occasional tinny moments don’t detract from what is widely regarded as one of the era’s standout performances.

ai_rating.rationale: Over 30 reviews are overwhelmingly positive (mostly 5‑star) praising both musical performance and sound quality; only a few mild criticisms appear, yielding an overall rating in the high‑four range.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Matrix blend praised as crisp and powerful; several reviewers note it is ‘mind blowing’ or ‘great sound’, with occasional comments about a slightly tinny SBD segment but no major drop‑outs.

show_quality.setlist_flow: First set is lauded as one of the strongest of the ’80s, maintaining relentless energy; second set sustains momentum with seamless segues (China→Rider, Estimated→Eyes) and a transcendent Other One that caps an already high‑octane night.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Repeatedly praised for fiery solos (Deal, To Lay Me Down), crisp tone and even ‘roasting’ the solo at the end of Deal; his vocals described as clear and emotionally powerful.
band_member_comments.Bob: Bob Weir’s vocal presence highlighted on Jack Straw and the “Jersey fillies” chant; his energy contributes to the overall hype.
band_member_comments.Keys: Brent (B3) receives accolades for soaring keyboard lines, especially on Half‑Step; keyboards noted as ‘killer’ throughout.
band_member_comments.Drums: Drum work praised in transitions like Drums→Space→The Other One; rhythm section described as tight and driving.
